title: Archie and Moonbeam's Moon Map
markdown:
Archie was a fluffy fluffy alpaca, like a cloud that had bounced down for a play. His wool was soft, soft, soft. Moonbeam was a silver pony. Her mane sparkled like water when the moon smiles down. They lived in a happy field. It was always sunny, always green, and smelled like yummy flowers. The grass tickled their noses when they went sniff, sniff, sniff. They loved to play tag.

One sunny day, a tiny star blinked hello. Then a map popped right between Archie’s ears and Moonbeam’s shiny mane. It was a moon map. It felt soft, like a whisper, and smelled like sleepy time.

“For you,” whispered the star. “It goes to a special place.”

Archie wiggled his nose. “A special place?” His voice was quiet, like a little breeze.

Moonbeam pranced. “Yes, yes,” she neighed. Her voice was like little water sounds splashing.

So Archie held the map in his mouth. It was soft and smooth. Moonbeam trotted next to him. The map had wiggly lines and little dots. It pointed to the biggest, roundest hill in the field. A hill that looked like a soft green pillow.

They walked past buzzy bees. The bees were busy, singing happy songs. They saw ants carrying crumbs. The ants were so busy they did not see Archie and Moonbeam walk by. The field was full of happy sounds: little birds singing tweet-tweet, leaves dancing in the wind, and a little stream going gurgle-gurgle. Archie and Moonbeam kept walking. The map glowed softly. They felt warm and happy, like a sunbeam hug.

They got to the top of the hill. The sun was bright and golden. Archie put the map down.

“We’re here,” he said.

But it looked just like their field, only from high up. It was pretty, but where was the special place?

Moonbeam nudged the map. Then Archie saw. The wiggly lines on the map looked like round bumps on the moon. And the little dots? They were sleepy stars, all snuggled up. The map was not pointing to a place to go. It was a map of the moon. It showed the moon when it was sleepy and quiet. It was a lovely surprise. It made their hearts feel full of happy wonder.

Archie looked at Moonbeam. Moonbeam looked at Archie. They giggled, a soft sound that floated on the breeze.

“It’s a moon map,” Archie whispered. “It shows sleepy stars.”

Moonbeam did a happy jump. “So pretty,” she said.

They knew this map was special. Its gentle glow should be shared. So they picked it up. Archie held it softly. Down the hill they went. They found Nia the bunny munching clover. Her nose wiggled. They found Squeaky the squirrel hiding a nut. His tail flicked.

“Look,” Archie said, his voice a little muffled. “A moon map.”

Moonbeam nudged it gently. “It shows the sleepy stars.”

All their friends came close. They looked at the map. They saw the round bumps and the twinkling dots. A quiet happy feeling spread. The moon map made a soft glow in the field. It made everyone’s hearts feel warm with friendship. As the sun went down, painting the sky soft colours, Archie and Moonbeam snuggled together. Their moon map was tucked safe. They dreamed of the moon and its quiet wonders. It was a perfect, perfect day.
